chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that
the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the testimony of women together with the oath of the claimant regarding a debt — he swears by God that his claim is indeed valid.

key_terms.الدَّيْن: Debt, a financial obligation or claim subject to legal adjudication
key_terms.الطَّالِب: The claimant or plaintiff who is pursuing a legal right or financial claim
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony, legal witness — one of the primary forms of evidence in Islamic law
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath sworn in God's name, used as legal corroboration in judicial proceedings

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women with an oath valid in debt claims according to Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports a legal ruling established by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family): in cases of financial debt, the testimony of women is admissible when combined with a corroborating oath by the claimant. The claimant must swear by God that his claim is a genuine right. This ruling reflects classical Islamic jurisprudence on evidence in financial disputes, where the combination of partial testimony and an oath (yamin) could substitute for a full two-witness requirement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> allowed the testimony of the women with an oath of the seeker regarding the debt, swearing by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that he is rightful for the right’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Urn ay r from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, accepted the testimony of women with the oath by the plaintiff in matters of loan. He swears by Allah that it is his right.’”
